Replace the performer in <Video 1> with the character defined by <Picture 2>.
<Picture 1> is a keyframe in which that same replacement has already been completed
— use it as the reference for the finished look.

Identity comes only from <Picture 2>: his face, bald head, skin tone, build, and the
yellow and purple basketball uniform with the number 24. Ignore everything else in
<Picture 2> — it is a multi-view character sheet on a plain white background, so never
render the white backdrop, the grid layout or the duplicated front / side / back views,
and never read them as several different people.

<Picture 1> supplies the finished costume and stage look: the same purple arm sleeves,
white socks and purple and gold sneakers, the same wet reflective stage floor, the same
backlit haze and the same rig and LED wall behind. <Picture 1> is a reference frame,
not the first frame — do not freeze the clip into its exact pose, its exact framing or
its exact camera height. Only its costume, lighting and stage dressing carry over.

<Video 1> supplies motion only. It gives the pose, blocking, body weight, timing and
camera movement — it supplies no identity and no costume at all.

He is the only person to be replaced. The four dancers in black uniforms, peaked caps
and sunglasses, the older white-haired dancer behind him and the drummer at the left
must all stay exactly as they are — not replaced, not recoloured, not restyled, not
removed and not duplicated. Do not mistake any of them for the target: they wear black
dance uniforms and dark glasses, whereas the target is the only man in a dark navy
Mao-style suit with a dark soft cap and a bare face.

Match his position, scale and movement from shot to shot. In the wide low-angle shot
he is not at the centre — he is the man off to the right of frame walking in with the
group. Follow him there rather than pulling him to the middle.

Keep the original cutting exactly. The clip is three separate shots cutting at about
0.9 seconds and about 2.2 seconds: preserve all three, in the same order, with the same
cut points. Do not merge them into one continuous shot and do not drop the middle one.

Preserve the camera, the wide stage, the haze, the backlit flares and the colour of the
stage lighting. Do not clean up or flatten the light.

Keep the source audio track unchanged.

No subtitles, no on-screen text, no bilibili watermark, no logo, no added graphics.

Negative: cartoon, anime, extra people, extra limbs, distorted hands, sunglasses, cap,
long hair, Mao suit carried over, text, subtitles, watermark, bilibili logo,
reference sheet, white background, duplicated body views, face morph, replaced dancer
